messages:
kevin: Heads up — getting multiple reports of alerts firing even though the Console charts show almost-zero traffic for the same window. Alert id ALRT-4312, metric inference.requests.latency.50p-rollup. Any ideas? :confused:

jen: Can you add the alert config and a quick screenshot of the chart and time range? Also the customer / org id so we can look up their audit context.

kevin: Screenshot pasted (link) — chart shows flat 0.0 for the 5m window, but alert triggered at 11:19 UTC. Alert config excerpt:
```yaml
metric: inference.requests.latency.50p-rollup
aggregation_window: 5m
aggregation_method: avg
threshold: > 200
evaluation_periods: 1
```
Customer: org-72. Also seeing this for another customer with a threshold on request_rate.

support-bot: Noted. Created support ticket SUP-1289 and pinned the logs.

matt: :eyes: I'll look at the rollup service. Any recent deploys around 11:18?

deploy-bot: rollup-service v2.14 deployed to prod at 2026-03-15T11:17:30Z by ci/cd (change: switch bucket alignment behavior).

matt: That deploy change stands out. Initial quick check in rollup logs shows some buckets shifted by a minute for a subset of hosts (rollup_offset missing). When an alert evaluates it sometimes picked up a partial bucket with a sudden transient due to delayed writes -> looks like false positive.

alice: To be explicit, the code change moved from truncating timestamps to the nearest alignment to flooring with a dynamic offset. For customers relying on fully-closed, aligned buckets the behavior changed.

kevin: That matches — the alert was evaluating against a bucket that contained only 30s of data from a spike, but the charting layer auto-smooths/omits partial buckets so Console showed 0.0.

sre-oncall: Short-term mitigation: set alerts to evaluate on the last completed bucket only, or require 2 consecutive buckets before firing. For example change to:
```yaml
evaluation_periods: 2
require_full_bucket: true  # internal flag we can enable per-alert
```
This prevents single-partial-bucket ghost alerts.

jen: Can we give customers a concrete repro step to validate?

matt: Repro steps I tested:
1) create a metric and emit 30s of high-rate events starting at 11:17:45 UTC.
2) Deploy rollup v2.14 behavior with rollup_offset not set (default removed).
3) Create a 5m aggregation alert with evaluation_periods=1.
Observed: alert fires at 11:19 while the Console chart (which collapses partial buckets) shows near-zero. Logs: attached snippet `rollup_service: bucket_start=11:15:00, partial=true, interval=5m, count=1200`.

alice: Root cause: change in default bucket alignment/offset in v2.14. Some hosts returned offsets they shouldn't have, producing misaligned rollup windows. Alert evaluation engine then compared against those partial buckets.

matt: Fix path: revert the alignment change or reintroduce default rollup_offset behavior. We're preparing a patch to enforce "evaluate only on sealed buckets" for alerts and to resume previous truncation semantics for rollups. Ticket: INF-5921.

jen: Temporary customer guidance: 1) toggle evaluation_periods to 2, 2) use require_full_bucket where available, 3) bump threshold slightly if immediate change not possible. I'll send a templated reply to affected orgs (SUP-1289).

kevin: Thanks — any ETA on the patch? Customers are worried about noise.

matt: ETA for hotfix: ~3 hours to rollback alignment change to a staged flag, ~24-48h for full rollout. I'll follow up in this thread with the rollup patch PR and the rollback ID.

support-bot: SUP-1289 updated with mitigation steps and engineering ticket INF-5921.

sre-oncall: Once patch is deployed we'll run a smoke test: emit controlled spikes and verify Console and alert engine agree on bucket boundaries.

kevin: Great. Please ping when the hotfix is live so I can notify the customers. :white_check_mark:

matt: Will do. Leaving notes in INF-5921 and will attach timeline and PR.

alice: Follow-up: we should add an integration test that enforces "alert evaluation uses only completed buckets" to avoid regressions. Adding to backlog.

kevin: Appreciated — closing loop once hotfix verifies.
